rules.permitted_development: On a qualifying agricultural unit in Scotland, agricultural buildings can be permitted development under Class 18, but designated landscapes carry tighter limits. In a national park, new agricultural buildings are generally limited to 465 square metres rather than 1,000 square metres, and siting and appearance are likely to face closer prior approval scrutiny.

rules.height_rules: In Cairngorms National Park, height is usually judged through landform and public views as much as through the numeric Class 18 ceiling, so a lower and simpler roof form is often the safer approach.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. The key checks are footprint, agricultural need and whether the building remains proportionate in a protected landscape.
rules.boundary_rules: Buildings should not be within 25 metres of a trunk or classified road. Access works, cut-and-fill and livestock separation from protected buildings can be just as important as the barn itself.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof allowance. Roof bulk, profile and finish remain part of the overall Class 18 judgement and can be scrutinised through prior approval.
rules.materials_rules: Use practical agricultural materials with subdued colours and low reflectivity. Prominent cladding and bright roofs are more likely to attract objection in protected landscapes.
